name: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule
full_name: HIPAA Breach Notification Rule: Notification in the Case of Breach of Unsecured Protected Health Information (45 CFR Part 164, Subpart D)
issuing_body: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)

sources.title: 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart D, Notification in the Case of Breach of Unsecured Protected Health Information
sources.publisher: eCFR, Office of the Federal Register

control_flags.requirement_type: standard, implementation_specification, or requirement (a duty the rule states without labelling it a standard: 164.412 and 164.414).
control_flags.parent: Implementation specifications only: the standard of the same section.
control_flags.objectives: The numbered paragraphs directly beneath a requirement. For 164.412 the two objectives are alternatives: which one applies depends on whether the law enforcement statement is written or oral.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable standards, implementation specifications and requirements that are implemented. The Breach Notification Rule itself defines no score; this percentage is an HCG measure of readiness to notify.

rules.summary: A requirement is met only when every element it lists is met.

An impermissible acquisition, access, use or disclosure of protected health information is presumed to be a breach unless a risk assessment of at least the four listed factors shows a low probability that the information was compromised.
rules.quote: is presumed to be a breach unless the covered entity or business associate, as applicable, demonstrates that there is a low probability that the protected health information has been compromised based on a risk assessment of at least the following factors:

rules.summary: Individuals are notified without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after the breach is discovered.
rules.quote: without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery of a breach.

rules.summary: A breach involving more than 500 residents of a State or jurisdiction also requires notice to prominent media outlets serving it.
rules.quote: For a breach of unsecured protected health information involving more than 500 residents of a State or jurisdiction, a covered entity shall, following the discovery of the breach as provided in § 164.404(a)(2), notify prominent media outlets serving the State or jurisdiction.

rules.summary: A breach involving 500 or more individuals is reported to the Secretary at the same time as individuals are notified.
rules.quote: provide the notification required by paragraph (a) of this section contemporaneously with the notice required by § 164.404(a) and in the manner specified on the HHS Web site.

rules.from: the end of the calendar year of discovery
rules.summary: Breaches involving fewer than 500 individuals are logged and reported to the Secretary no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar year in which they were discovered.
rules.quote: not later than 60 days after the end of each calendar year, provide the notification required by paragraph (a) of this section for breaches discovered during the preceding calendar year

rules.from: discovery of the breach by the business associate
rules.summary: A business associate notifies the covered entity without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after it discovers the breach.
rules.quote: a business associate shall provide the notification required by paragraph (a) of this section without unreasonable delay and in no case later than 60 calendar days after discovery of a breach.

rules.summary: The covered entity or business associate carries the burden of showing that every required notification was made, or that the use or disclosure was not a breach.
rules.quote: shall have the burden of demonstrating that all notifications were made as required by this subpart or that the use or disclosure did not constitute a breach, as defined at § 164.402.

glossary.definition: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, whose Breach Notification Rule requires notice when unsecured protected health information is breached.
Protected health information: individually identifiable health information held or transmitted by a covered entity or its business associate.
Protected health information that has not been made unusable, unreadable or indecipherable to unauthorized persons through a technology or methodology specified by the Secretary.
U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, which issues and enforces the HIPAA rules through its Office for Civil Rights (OCR).
A person or organization that creates, receives, maintains or transmits protected health information on behalf of a covered entity.
